sources.title: Digest of Education Statistics 2023, Table 205.80: Private elementary and secondary schools, enrollment, teachers, and high school graduates, by state
sources.notes: Private counts rounded to nearest 10 by NCES. Covers 50 states + DC only (PSS does not survey territories). Excludes private prekindergarten-only schools; K-12 column excludes PK pupils.

sources.title: Digest of Education Statistics 2022, Table 203.40: Enrollment in public elementary and secondary schools, by level, grade, and state or jurisdiction: Fall 2021
sources.notes: publicK12 computed = total all grades - prekindergarten (includes ungraded and grade 13). US row includes BIE and DoDEA. Territories rows: Guam, N. Marianas, Puerto Rico, USVI present; American Samoa not available.

sources.title: Condition of Education: Private School Enrollment (indicator cgc)
sources.notes: States 4.7 million K-12 private students = 9 percent of combined public+private in fall 2019 and fall 2021; state range 2 percent (Wyoming, Utah) to 20 percent (DC). Fall 2021 orientation counts: Catholic 1.7M, other religious 2.0M, nonsectarian 1.1M. Private-student poverty rate 11 percent vs 17 percent public.

sources.title: Digest of Education Statistics 2022, Table 206.10: Number and percentage of homeschooled students ages 5 through 17 with a grade equivalent of K-12
sources.notes: 2019 excludes students enrolled in school more than 24 hours/week.

sources.title: Digest of Education Statistics 2022, Table 206.30: Percentage distribution of students enrolled in grades 1 through 12, by public school type and charter status, private school orientation, and selected child and household characteristics: 2019
sources.notes: Column percentages (composition of each school type). Private school total = 9.2% of enrolled grade 1-12 students (religious 7.4%, nonsectarian 1.8%). Excludes homeschoolers.

sources.title: School Choice in the United States: 2019 (NCES 2019-106), Indicator 5 Homeschooling
sources.notes: 3.3 percent of ages 5-17 K-12 homeschooled in 2016, up from 1.7 percent in 1999.

sources.title: American Community Survey 2024 1-year, Table B14002 Sex by school enrollment by level of school by type of school (retrieved via Census Reporter API, which mirrors Census ACS data)
sources.table: B14002 (kindergarten, grades 1-4, 5-8, 9-12; public vs private, both sexes summed)
sources.notes: Official api.census.gov now requires a key and refused the request. ACS 'private' includes homeschooled children (ACS questionnaire groups home school with private), so ACS private shares run higher than PSS: US ACS K-12 private share 13.4% vs PSS/CCD 9.0%.

sources.title: Pew Research Center, Religion, fertility and child-rearing (2023-24 Religious Landscape Study)
sources.notes: Not federal. Combines homeschool with private religious school; no per-denomination private rates published.

PR.notes: Computed from ACS B14002 K + grades 1-12, public vs private, males+females. Not comparable with state PSS figures: ACS private includes homeschool and is a survey estimate (ACS US-level same method gives 13.4% vs 9.0% PSS). CCD fall 2021 public K-12 for PR = 257,539 (Table 203.40); no NCES private count for PR.

GU.notes: Public K-12 only (total 28,402 minus PK 663). No federal private count found.

MP.notes: Public K-12 only (9,491 minus PK 290). No federal private count found.

VI.notes: Public K-12 only (10,234 minus PK 89). No federal private count found.

AS.notes: CCD reports 'Not available' for American Samoa.

nationalPrivateShare.notes: Computed 4,731,300 / (4,731,300 + 48,022,538). Matches Condition of Education's stated 9 percent (coe-private). NHES 2019 survey gives 9.2% of grade 1-12 enrolled students (nhes-206.30); ACS 2024 gives 13.4% but counts homeschool as private.

homeschoolShare.notes: 2.8% (SE 0.18) of ages 5-17, K-12 grade equivalent; 1,457 thousand students. 2016: 3.3% (school-choice-2019 / 206.10); 2012: 3.4%; 1999: 1.7%. 2019 by household income: <=$20k 3.0%, $20-50k 2.5%, $50-75k 3.6%, $75-100k 3.2%, >$100k 2.5%. Two parents with one in labor force: 6.6%. Rural 4.7%. Post-2020 federal figure not found (Census Household Pulse showed a pandemic spike but is experimental).

privateShareByIncome.notes: Computed: 0.092 (private share of enrolled grades 1-12) x 0.096 (share of private students who are poor) / 0.165 (share of all students who are poor). Source text: private students 8% poor in 2016 (School Choice 2019, Indicator 4).
Computed by same Bayes step from column distribution (private 7.9% vs all 18.9%)

privateShareByReligion.note: No federal source gives private attendance by family religion (NHES and ACS do not ask religion). Closest figures:

schoolOrientation.group: religious private schools, share of all enrolled grade 1-12 students
nonsectarian private schools, share of all enrolled grade 1-12 students
Catholic schools, share of private K-12 students
schoolOrientation.notes: Computed 1.7M/4.7M from rounded counts (orientation counts include PK-capable schools; CoE rounding)

schoolOrientation.group: other religious schools, share of private K-12 students
nonsectarian schools, share of private K-12 students
schoolOrientation.notes: Computed 1.1M/4.7M; the three sum to ~1.02 due to rounding

byParentReligiosity.group: all parents of minor children: homeschool or private religious school
Christian parents: homeschool or private religious school
highly religious parents: homeschool or private religious school

gaps: Private K-12 counts for Guam, N. Marianas, USVI, American Samoa: PSS covers only 50 states + DC; ACS does not cover Island Areas; the 2020 Island Areas Census DHC/DP2 tables on data.census.gov were not checked table-by-table (api.census.gov now requires a key).
Puerto Rico share is ACS-based (includes homeschool, survey estimate) and not directly comparable to the PSS/CCD state figures; scale or treat as an upper bound.

Private share by detailed household income dollar bands not published for 2019; only poverty status (computed shares from column distributions in Table 206.30). Raw shares by income band would need NHES 2019 public-use microdata.

Private attendance by family religion (Catholic, evangelical, Jewish, etc.): no federal source; Pew 2023-24 gives only combined homeschool+private-religious rates for all/Christian/highly religious parents.
State counts are fall 2021 (latest PSS by state in Digest 2023); PSS 2023-24 state tables not yet checked.
State private counts are rounded to tens and some states carry sampling SE (e.g., OK SE 5,050; AZ 7,525; DE 5,241 in PSS area-frame estimates).
